experiences.name: Mercado de San Juan Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore one of Mexico City's most beloved gourmet markets, sampling exotic cheeses, fresh seafood tostadas, traditional tacos, and artisanal products. Chat with local vendors and taste authentic Mexican flavors in a vibrant market atmosphere.

experiences.name: Teotihuacan Pyramids & Street Food Experience
experiences.description: Visit the ancient pre-Aztec city of Teotihuacan, climb the Pyramid of the Sun and Moon, and explore the Avenue of the Dead. On the way back, stop at a local roadside stand for authentic tlayudas and pulque, a traditional fermented agave drink.
experiences.location: Teotihuacan, State of Mexico (day trip from Mexico City)

experiences.name: Coyoacán Neighborhood & Frida Kahlo Museum
experiences.description: Wander through the charming cobblestone streets of Coyoacán, visit the iconic Casa Azul (Frida Kahlo Museum), browse artisan crafts at the local market, and enjoy a traditional Mexican lunch at a neighborhood cantina with dishes like chiles en nogada.

experiences.name: Tacos al Pastor Crawl in Roma & Condesa
experiences.description: Embark on a self-guided taco crawl through the trendy Roma and Condesa neighborhoods, hitting legendary taquería spots known for their spit-roasted al pastor, suadero, and carnitas tacos. Pair with agua fresca or a cold Mexican beer at each stop.

experiences.name: Palacio de Bellas Artes & Historic Center Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore the stunning Art Nouveau Palacio de Bellas Artes, admire Diego Rivera's famous murals inside, then walk through the historic Zócalo square, visit the Metropolitan Cathedral, and discover the ruins of the Templo Mayor — a powerful blend of colonial and indigenous history.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Mexico City
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Use this time to rest on the plane and prepare for arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at ACDMX airport at 13:00. Take the Metro Line 5 from Terminal Aérea station to get to Centro Histórico (cheapest option, ~$0.50 USD). Check in to your boutique stay in Centro Histórico. Once settled, take a relaxed walk around the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución) — the main square and heart of the city. Admire the Metropolitan Cathedral and the National Palace exterior for free.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Calle Regina, a lively pedestrian street in Centro Histórico full of street food stalls and local energy. Explore the area around Mercado de Artesanías and soak in the neighborhood atmosphere as the city lights up at night.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick snack at the airport.
meals.lunch: Stop at a street taco stand near the Zócalo — look for tacos de canasta or tacos al pastor for around $0.50–$1 USD each. Try 3–4 tacos for a filling and authentic first meal.
meals.dinner: Head to Calle Regina for gorditas or tlayudas from street vendors (~$3–5 USD total). Wash it down with a fresh agua fresca from a local stand.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the afternoon arrival. Use the evening to orient yourself and get comfortable with the neighborhood. Keep pesos handy — many street vendors don't accept cards. Exchange currency at a bank or ATM (avoid airport exchange booths for better rates).

day_by_day.morning: Start the day early at Mercado de San Juan (open from 9am), a beloved local market just minutes from Centro Histórico. Browse stalls selling fresh produce, cheeses, meats, and international goods. Then walk to the nearby Palacio de Bellas Artes — admire the stunning Art Nouveau exterior and check out the free exhibitions in the lobby. Head upstairs to the mural hall (small entry fee ~$1–2 USD) to see masterpieces by Diego Rivera and David Alfaro Siqueiros.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along Avenida Madero (a pedestrian-only street) toward the Zócalo. Enter the Templo Mayor archaeological site and museum (~$4 USD) — the ruins of the ancient Aztec capital Tenochtitlán sit right in the heart of the city. Afterward, climb to the free viewing terrace on the top floor of the nearby Suprema Corte de Justicia to see more Rivera murals at no cost.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Plaza Garibaldi, about 15 minutes on foot from Centro, to hear Mariachi bands play in the open square — a quintessential Mexico City experience. The atmosphere is especially lively on weekday evenings. Grab street food from the surrounding stalls.

meals.breakfast: Eat at Mercado de San Juan — try fresh juices, tamales, or chilaquiles from market stalls (~$2–4 USD).
meals.lunch: Grab comida corrida (a fixed-price set lunch) at a local fondita near the Zócalo. These typically include soup, a main dish, rice, beans, and a drink for ~$4–6 USD — the best budget deal in Mexico City.
meals.dinner: Enjoy street food at or near Plaza Garibaldi — pozole, tacos, or tostadas from vendors (~$3–5 USD total).

day_by_day.notes: Templo Mayor is closed on Mondays, so Tuesday is perfect. Comida corrida is served roughly 1pm–4pm and is the best value meal of the day — look for handwritten signs saying 'Comida Corrida' outside small local restaurants.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro to Coyoacán (~45 min, $0.50 USD), one of Mexico City's most charming and bohemian neighborhoods. Visit the Frida Kahlo Museum (Casa Azul) — book tickets online in advance (~$12 USD, one of the pricier but most worthwhile stops). Wander the colorful cobblestone streets and admire the colonial architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Mercado de Coyoacán, a bustling local market where you can find handcrafts, fresh food, and the famous tostadas de tinga. Stroll around Jardín Centenario and Plaza Hidalgo, Coyoacán's central squares, where locals relax and street performers entertain. Browse artisan stalls for affordable souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico via Metro. Walk through the historic streets around Calle Donceles, known as the 'Street of Used Books,' lined with second-hand bookshops. Enjoy a quiet evening exploring your neighborhood and picking up snacks from local tiendas.

meals.breakfast: Before heading out, grab pan dulce (sweet bread) and café de olla from a local panadería near your hotel (~$1–2 USD).
meals.lunch: Eat at Mercado de Coyoacán — try tostadas de tinga, enchiladas, or fresh ceviche from market stalls (~$3–5 USD). This is one of the best food market experiences in the city.
meals.dinner: Back in Centro, find a local taquería for tacos de guisado (stewed filling tacos) — hearty, cheap, and delicious (~$3–4 USD for a full meal).

day_by_day.notes: Book Frida Kahlo Museum tickets well in advance online as they sell out quickly. The Metro is the fastest and cheapest way to get to Coyoacán — take Line 3 (green) to Viveros station. Coyoacán is very walkable once you arrive.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early Metro ride to Chapultepec Park — one of the largest urban parks in the world and a beloved green lung of the city (free entry). Walk through the forested paths and visit Lago de Chapultepec. Climb up to Chapultepec Castle (Castillo de Chapultepec), a stunning hilltop palace with panoramic views of the city (~$3 USD entry). The castle houses the National Museum of History with impressive murals and imperial artifacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk from Chapultepec toward the upscale Colonia Roma neighborhood (~20 min walk or short Metro ride). Explore the tree-lined streets, Art Deco architecture, and independent coffee shops. Visit Parque México and Parque España, two beautiful neighborhood parks popular with locals. Browse the street art and murals scattered throughout the colonia.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Mercado de Medellín in Roma for an authentic local market experience with food stalls, produce, and a lively atmosphere. Then take the Metro back to Centro Histórico for the night.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at a street stand near Chapultepec — tamales and atole (a warm corn-based drink) are a classic and filling combo (~$2 USD).
meals.lunch: Eat comida corrida at a fondita in Colonia Roma (~$5–6 USD). Roma has excellent local restaurants with great value set lunches.
meals.dinner: Try tacos de suadero or barbacoa from a well-regarded street taquería in Centro Histórico (~$3–4 USD). Ask locals for their favorite spot — they'll never steer you wrong.

day_by_day.notes: Chapultepec Park is free but the castle requires a ticket. The park is especially lively on weekends — on weekdays it's more peaceful and less crowded. Roma is a safe and walkable neighborhood great for leisurely afternoon exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Spend your final morning revisiting your favorite spots in Centro Histórico at a slower pace. Visit the Museo del Estanquillo (free entry on Sundays, ~$1–2 on other days) — a charming museum dedicated to Mexico City's popular culture and history. Walk through the historic Palacio de Correos (Postal Palace), a gorgeous early 20th-century building open to the public for free — admire the ornate interior.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Mercado de La Merced, one of the largest traditional markets in Latin America, just a short walk from Centro. Immerse yourself in the sensory overload of hundreds of stalls selling spices, herbs, produce, street food, and everyday goods. This is the most authentic market experience in the city and completely free to explore. Pick up last-minute snacks or small souvenirs like dried chiles, vanilla, or Mexican chocolate.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a final dinner in Centro Histórico. Treat yourself to a sit-down meal at a local Mexican restaurant — look for spots serving mole, chiles en nogada (if in season), or pozole. End the night with a mezcal or michelada at a local cantina for a true farewell to Mexico City.

meals.breakfast: Visit a local panadería or market stall for fresh churros with chocolate dipping sauce — a classic Mexico City breakfast treat (~$1–2 USD).
meals.lunch: Eat at Mercado de La Merced — choose from dozens of food stalls offering everything from soups to antojitos. Budget ~$3–5 USD for a generous and authentic meal.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on your last night — a full sit-down meal with a drink at a well-regarded local Mexican restaurant in Centro Histórico should still cost ~$10–15 USD, excellent value for a memorable farewell meal.

day_by_day.notes: La Merced market is best visited in the morning or early afternoon when it's most active. Keep an eye on your belongings in busy market areas. If your flight home is the next day, pack your bags tonight and confirm transportation to the airport — the Metro is again the most budget-friendly option.

trip_options.title: Classic Mexico City Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Check in to your boutique hotel in Centro Histórico, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely walk around the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), one of the largest city squares in the world. Visit the exterior of the Palacio Nacional and the Metropolitan Cathedral. Stroll down Madero Street, a pedestrian boulevard lined with colonial architecture, street performers, and local vendors.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Templo Mayor archaeological site area for the golden-hour atmosphere, then explore the lit-up Centro Histórico streets. Visit the iconic Palacio de Bellas Artes from the outside to admire its stunning Art Nouveau facade illuminated at night.

meals.lunch: Grab a quick but authentic bite at Mercado de San Juan nearby — try a torta or taco at one of the market stalls for around 80–150 MXN.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Café de Tacuba, a historic restaurant open since 1912 in Centro Histórico. Try classic Mexican dishes like enchiladas or chiles en nogada. Mid-range pricing around 250–400 MXN per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep luggage light for the afternoon walk. Wear comfortable shoes — the Centro is best explored on foot. Exchange currency or use ATMs near the hotel for local pesos.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Templo Mayor Museum (open from 9:00 AM) — the ancient Aztec temple ruins right in the heart of Centro Histórico. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring the excavated ruins and the excellent on-site museum showcasing Mexica artifacts. Entry fee around 85 MXN.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Palacio Nacional to see Diego Rivera's famous murals depicting Mexican history — free entry with ID. Afterward, explore the nearby Barrio Chino (Chinatown) area and walk along República de Uruguay street for local market shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Plaza Garibaldi, about 15 minutes walk from the hotel, to experience Mariachi culture — musicians gather here every evening. Enjoy the lively atmosphere and street food around the plaza.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or a nearby café such as El Cardenal (Centro branch) — try chilaquiles or tamales with café de olla. Budget around 120–200 MXN.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local fondita (small family restaurant) near Templo Mayor — look for a comida corrida (set lunch menu) with soup, main course, and drink for around 100–160 MXN.
meals.dinner: Dinner near Plaza Garibaldi at Salón Tenampa, a traditional cantina with live Mariachi. Try birria or pozole with a mezcal or beer. Budget around 300–450 MXN per person.

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Templo Mayor early to beat crowds. Bring a small backpack with water and sunscreen. Plaza Garibaldi is liveliest after 8 PM — keep an eye on your belongings in busy areas.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro or an Uber (15–25 minutes) to Coyoacán neighborhood. Visit the Frida Kahlo Museum (Casa Azul) — book tickets online in advance as they sell out quickly. Entry around 270 MXN. Spend 1.5 hours exploring the iconic blue house and its collections.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wander through Coyoacán's charming cobblestone streets and visit the Jardín Centenario and Plaza Hidalgo. Browse the weekend artisan market stalls for local crafts, textiles, and souvenirs. Visit the Mercado de Coyoacán for snacks and local products.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico and explore the Eje Central area. Visit the Museo de Arte Popular (MAP) if open late, or enjoy a mezcal tasting at a local mezcalería in the neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast near the hotel before heading out — try a street-side taquería for tacos de canasta or a torta. Budget around 60–100 MXN.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Coyoacán at Los Danzantes restaurant or a market stall inside Mercado de Coyoacán — try tostadas de tinga or memelas. Budget 150–250 MXN.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Azul Histórico in Centro Histórico — a beautiful courtyard restaurant serving refined Mexican regional cuisine. Budget around 350–500 MXN per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Frida Kahlo Museum tickets at least 1–2 weeks in advance at museofridakahlo.org.mx. Coyoacán is especially vibrant on weekends. Use Metro Line 3 (green) to Viveros station for an affordable and authentic transit experience.

day_by_day.morning: Take an Uber or organized tour (30–40 minutes) to Teotihuacán — the ancient pre-Columbian city with the famous Pyramids of the Sun and Moon. Arrive early (site opens at 9:00 AM) to climb the Pyramid of the Sun before crowds and heat build up. Entry around 90 MXN.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Teotihuacán — walk the Avenue of the Dead, visit the Temple of Quetzalcóatl, and explore the on-site museum. Head back to Mexico City by 3–4 PM. Stop briefly at Plaza de las Tres Culturas in Tlatelolco on the way back if energy allows.
day_by_day.evening: Relax evening in Centro Histórico. Take a night walk along the illuminated Paseo de la Reforma or enjoy a rooftop bar with views of the city skyline.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before departure — grab pan dulce (sweet bread) and café de olla from a street vendor near the hotel. Budget around 40–70 MXN.
meals.lunch: Lunch near Teotihuacán site at one of the local restaurants outside the main entrance — try barbacoa tacos or mole dishes. Budget around 150–250 MXN.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a rooftop restaurant in Centro Histórico such as Terraza Catedral — enjoy city views with Mexican fusion cuisine. Budget around 300–450 MXN per person.

day_by_day.notes: Wear very comfortable shoes, a hat, and sunscreen for Teotihuacán — it involves significant walking and climbing. Bring at least 1.5 liters of water per person. Consider hiring a local guide at the entrance for deeper historical context (around 300–500 MXN for a 2-hour tour).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Palacio de Bellas Artes interior — see the stunning Art Deco architecture and Diego Rivera, José Clemente Orozco, and David Alfaro Siqueiros murals inside. Entry to the main hall is free; museum galleries around 90 MXN. Spend 1.5 hours exploring.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Alameda Central park for a relaxing stroll through one of the oldest urban parks in the Americas. Visit the nearby Museo Mural Diego Rivera (entry around 45 MXN) to see the famous 'Dream of a Sunday Afternoon in Alameda Park' mural. Do last-minute souvenir shopping in the surrounding streets.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Mexico City — enjoy a farewell dinner in the Centro Histórico, then take a relaxing evening stroll through the Zócalo one last time, soaking in the atmosphere of this historic square lit up at night.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at El Cardenal on Palma Street — one of Mexico City's most beloved breakfast institutions. Try the tamales, pan dulce, and hot chocolate. Budget around 150–250 MXN.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Mercado de San Juan — build your own meal from the diverse stalls offering cheeses, meats, fresh juices, and international bites. Budget around 120–200 MXN.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Contramar or a highly-rated local restaurant in Centro — splurge slightly on a memorable final meal with Mexican seafood or traditional mole. Budget around 400–600 MXN per person.

day_by_day.notes: Check departure logistics and confirm transportation to the airport in advance. Centro Histórico is very walkable — most Day 5 activities are within a 15-minute walk of each other. Consider buying locally made crafts or artisan goods as souvenirs rather than tourist shops for better quality and fair prices.

trip_options.title: Premium Mexico City Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Mexico City International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private transfer arranged from airport to boutique hotel in Centro Histórico via luxury chauffeur service.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in and freshen up at the boutique hotel. Begin a leisurely private guided walking tour of the immediate Centro Histórico neighborhood: visit the iconic Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), admire the Palacio Nacional and its stunning Diego Rivera murals, and stroll along the pedestrian corridor of Madero Street.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset visit to the rooftop terrace of a nearby historic building for panoramic views of the Zócalo. Followed by a welcome dinner at a renowned fine-dining restaurant in Centro Histórico celebrating contemporary Mexican haute cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or airport meal prior to landing
meals.lunch: Light welcome snack and artisanal beverages upon hotel check-in, arranged by the concierge
meals.dinner: Dinner at Azul Histórico — elegant courtyard restaurant offering refined Mexican regional dishes, excellent mezcal selection, and a curated wine list

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Keep Day 1 relaxed to allow for jet lag adjustment. Hotel concierge should be briefed on dietary preferences before arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Templo Mayor archaeological site and its world-class museum, exploring the Aztec ceremonial center unearthed beneath the city. Includes a dedicated expert archaeologist guide for an in-depth cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Palacio de Bellas Artes to admire its stunning Art Nouveau and Art Deco architecture and rotating fine art exhibitions. Afterward, explore the historic Mercado de San Juan — a premium gourmet market beloved by chefs — for tastings of artisan cheeses, charcuterie, exotic fruits, and regional delicacies.
day_by_day.evening: Private mezcal and tequila tasting experience at a curated spirits bar in the Centro, guided by a certified sommelier. Followed by dinner at a celebrated chef's table experience featuring traditional Oaxacan and Mexico City-inspired tasting menus.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet in-hotel breakfast featuring chilaquiles, fresh tropical fruits, pan dulce, and specialty Mexican coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet tasting lunch at Mercado de San Juan — curated bites from premium vendors including imported cheeses, fresh ceviche, and artisan bread
meals.dinner: Dinner at Contramar or equivalent — iconic Mexico City seafood restaurant known for its tuna tostadas and grilled fish al pastor, reservations essential

day_by_day.notes: Book Templo Mayor private guide at least 48 hours in advance. Palacio de Bellas Artes may have ticketed exhibitions — confirm schedule with concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer to the borough of Coyoacán for a deeply cultural morning. Visit the Frida Kahlo Museum (La Casa Azul) with a skip-the-line private access booking. Explore the cobblestone streets, colorful colonial architecture, and vibrant local plazas of this bohemian neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the nearby San Ángel neighborhood for a visit to the Museo Casa Estudio Diego Rivera y Frida Kahlo and the Saturday Bazar del Sábado art market (if applicable to date). Return to Centro Histórico via private vehicle, with a stop at the iconic UNAM campus to admire its UNESCO World Heritage murals and architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private tasting dinner experience at Pujol (one of Latin America's top-ranked restaurants), featuring Chef Enrique Olvera's legendary mole madre and innovative Mexican tasting menu. Advance reservation is essential and highly recommended.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — eggs motuleños, fresh-pressed juices, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Leisurely lunch at El Cardenal de Coyoacán or a charming local bistro in Coyoacán Plaza — traditional Mexican comfort food in an authentic setting
meals.dinner: Pujol — world-renowned tasting menu restaurant; request wine pairing for the full premium experience

day_by_day.notes: Frida Kahlo Museum requires advance timed-entry tickets — book weeks ahead as it sells out quickly. Pujol reservations should be made at least 1–2 months in advance. Private driver recommended for the full day.

day_by_day.morning: Private half-day excursion to the ancient pyramids of Teotihuacán (approximately 1 hour from Centro Histórico by private vehicle). Enjoy an exclusive early-access sunrise or morning visit before crowds arrive, guided by a certified archaeologist. Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon and walk the Avenue of the Dead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mexico City. Stop in the upscale Polanco neighborhood for a leisurely afternoon exploring high-end boutiques, galleries, and the prestigious Museo Soumaya — home to one of Latin America's finest private art collections with works by Rodin, Dalí, and Monet, free of charge.
day_by_day.evening: Cocktail hour at a sophisticated rooftop bar in Polanco or Roma Norte with skyline views. Dinner at a premium contemporary Mexican restaurant in Polanco, celebrated for its creative interpretations of regional Mexican flavors.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel before departure — fresh fruit, yogurt, granola, and coffee to go
meals.lunch: Late lunch at La Gruta Restaurant inside a natural cave at Teotihuacán — a truly unique dining experience with traditional Mexican cuisine in an extraordinary setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Quintonil — Chef Jorge Vallejo's acclaimed restaurant in Polanco, ranked among the world's best; celebrated for its use of indigenous ingredients and seasonal Mexican produce

day_by_day.notes: Depart for Teotihuacán by 7:00–7:30 AM to beat the heat and crowds. Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring sun protection. Museo Soumaya is free entry. Quintonil reservations must be made well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Immersive private Mexican cooking class with a celebrated local chef in a traditional kitchen setting in Centro Histórico or Roma neighborhood. Learn to prepare classic dishes such as mole negro, tamales, and agua fresca from scratch using market-fresh ingredients sourced that morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final cultural exploration: visit the stunning Museo Nacional de Antropología in Chapultepec Park — one of the world's greatest anthropology museums, housing the Aztec Sun Stone and extraordinary pre-Columbian collections. Stroll through the lush Bosque de Chapultepec, Mexico City's premier urban park.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell luxury dinner at a celebrated rooftop or fine-dining restaurant in Roma Norte or Condesa — Mexico City's trendiest cultural districts. Toast to the journey with a premium Mexican wine or aged mezcal selection.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel gourmet breakfast — full spread including molletes, fresh juices, and specialty coffee before the cooking class
meals.lunch: Eat the dishes prepared during the morning cooking class — a hands-on, intimate, and memorable culinary experience
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Rosetta — Chef Elena Reygadas' iconic Roma Norte restaurant, celebrated for its blend of Italian and Mexican influences, fresh pasta, and seasonal ingredients; James Beard Award-winning chef

day_by_day.notes: Cooking class should be booked in advance through a reputable culinary school or private chef service. Museo Nacional de Antropología requires at least 2–3 hours; consider a private guide for an enriched experience. Confirm any departure logistics with hotel concierge for the following day.
